submissions.findingTextShort: Current FDA guidance says CBD products are excluded from the federal dietary-supplement definition, conflicting with permissive legal/recommendation defaults on the held profile.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: FDA's current cannabis/CBD regulatory guidance states that, based on available evidence, THC and CBD products are excluded from the dietary-supplement definition under section 201(ff)(3)(B) of the FD&C Act and that FDA has not issued a regulation overriding that exclusion. The current Cannabidiol profile is NOINDEX but still exposes legalRisk none, monetizationAllowed true, recommendationAllowed true, and no required human review. This finding records that dated U.S. federal regulatory-governance mismatch without deciding individualized legal advice or state-law status.
submissions.usageContext: Authoritative U.S. FDA regulatory-status provenance; not efficacy evidence and not individualized legal advice.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Regulatory state is jurisdiction- and time-dependent and requires dated authoritative revalidation.

submissions.findingTextShort: FDA approval of purified-CBD Epidiolex for specified seizure indications is product- and indication-specific and cannot be inherited by unapproved consumer CBD products.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: FDA identifies Epidiolex, a purified cannabidiol prescription drug, as an approved cannabis-derived drug product for specified seizure indications. That approval establishes a product-, formulation-, dose-, population-, and indication-specific evidence identity. Retail CBD oils, gummies, foods, products marketed as supplements, and other unapproved CBD products must not inherit that approval or its clinical efficacy by molecule-name overlap.
submissions.populationContext: FDA-approved prescription-product indications rather than general wellness use.
submissions.usageContext: Epidiolex/purified prescription CBD product boundary; not generic consumer CBD efficacy.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This finding does not import Epidiolex dosing or adverse-event rates into unrelated preparations.

submissions.findingTextShort: FDA consumer guidance identifies liver injury, drug-interaction, and additive sedation concerns for CBD while emphasizing major unknowns around unapproved products.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: FDA consumer guidance states that CBD can cause liver injury, can affect the action of other drugs, and can increase sedation or drowsiness when combined with alcohol or other CNS depressants. FDA also emphasizes that unapproved CBD products have not undergone the same product-specific evaluation for effectiveness, dosing, interactions, and safety as an approved drug. These are authoritative safety/governance signals, not a universal incidence estimate or proof that every CBD preparation has the same risk magnitude.
submissions.usageContext: General FDA consumer-safety context for CBD products; route, formulation, exposure and co-medications remain material.
submissions.safetyContext: Liver, drug-interaction and CNS-sedation concerns require product/exposure-specific clinical receipts for quantitative claims.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The FDA warning does not establish a single safe dose or uniform risk rate across consumer products.

submissions.findingTextShort: The live Cannabidiol profile still reports Grade B and material safety language while exposing zero canonical source receipts and an empty claim map.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: On current main after the healthy-adult CBD safety meta-analysis was separately registered and governed, public/data/compounds-detail/cannabidiol.json still exposes sourceCount 0 and an empty claimMap while its summary reports Grade B, its safety text names diarrhea, fatigue/sedation, CYP3A4/CYP2C19 interactions and dose-dependent liver-enzyme elevation, and governance permits recommendation and monetization despite NOINDEX/needs_review. Material clinical and regulatory propositions should remain reconstructable from attested source/claim receipts rather than unsourced prose or mechanism count.
submissions.usageContext: Current-main evidence-receipt and recommendation-governance conflict; no public mutation in this fragment.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The already-governed PMID 41789242 safety meta-analysis is deliberately not restaged here; this finding concerns unresolved public/canonical propagation and regulatory provenance.
